## Comparability caveat

Alaska Air Group's FY2024 figures are **not** directly comparable to its own prior years or to the other four carriers. Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward, contributing **$869 million of revenue** in the stub period [DOC-2]. Alaska's headline FY2024 growth is therefore partly inorganic and reflects only ~3.5 months of the acquired business (FY2025 will carry a further full-year step-up). The other four carriers are clean, calendar-year, like-for-like comparisons [DOC-1].

## Growth calculations

| Carrier | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY24 YoY | FY22→FY24 (2-yr CAGR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $50,582M | $58,048M | $61,643M | +6.2% | +21.9% (10.4%) |
| United | $44,955M | $53,717M | $57,063M | **+6.2%** | **+26.9% (12.7%)** |
| Southwest | $23,814M | $26,091M | $27,483M | +5.3% | +15.4% (7.4%) |
| American | $48,971M | $52,788M | $54,211M | +2.7% | +10.7% (5.2%) |
| Alaska (as reported) | $9,646M | $10,426M | $11,735M | +12.6% | +21.7% (10.3%) |
| Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $9,646M | $10,426M | ~$10,866M | ~+4.2% | ~+12.7% (6.1%) |

All revenue figures from [DOC-1]; the $869M Hawaiian adjustment from [DOC-2].

## Assessment

- **Alaska's apparent +12.6% YoY is misleading.** Stripping out the $869M of acquired Hawaiian revenue [DOC-2] leaves roughly +4.2% organic growth, which would rank it **fourth** of five, behind Southwest.
- **United is the strongest on an organic basis.** It posted the highest FY2024 YoY growth (+6.23% vs. Delta's +6.19%) and by a wide margin the best two-year trajectory, +26.9% versus Delta's +21.9%, Southwest's +15.4%, and American's +10.7% [DOC-1].
- **Delta is a close second**, essentially tied on FY2024 YoY but recovering from a higher FY2022 base.
- **American is clearly the laggard**, with growth decelerating to +2.7% in FY2024 [DOC-1].

Caveat: these are top-line revenue figures only; they say nothing about margin quality, and United's superior two-year growth partly reflects a lower FY2022 starting base ($44,955M vs. Delta's $50,582M) as international and business travel recovered [DOC-1].

ANSWER: United Airlines Holdings — highest FY2024 revenue growth (+6.2% YoY, narrowly ahead of Delta) and clearly the best FY2022–FY2024 trajectory (+26.9%, a 12.7% CAGR). Alaska's headline +12.6% is not comparable because it includes $869M from the Hawaiian acquisition closed September 18, 2024; excluding that, Alaska grew only ~4.2%.
